subject: Clarifying PHI/PII retention caps and redaction options - Next steps
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@healixhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Kumar <asha.kumar@healixhealth.com>

Subject: Clarifying PHI/PII retention caps and redaction options - Next steps

Irene,

Thanks for taking time earlier. Asha and I pulled together our immediate compliance asks so we can compare to Redwood's default behaviors and decide whether we need a Private deployment or specific contractual controls. High level: we need firm answers on maximum retention for PHI and PII, deletion guarantees (including backups/snapshots), and whether we can apply deterministic redaction patterns before data reaches model weights (or ensure model never sees raw PHI).

Specifics:
- Our regulator expects no PHI persisted beyond 180 days unless explicitly consented or legally required (audit requirement: 7 years for some records). We’d prefer a default 90-day cap on production test data. Can Redwood enforce retention caps by data class?
- If we request a purge, what is the SLA to completely remove data from hot stores, caches (KV), and backups? Does that vary by Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
- Regarding redaction: options we’re considering are client-side field stripping, deterministic hashing (pseudonymization), server-side redaction on ingest, and inference-time masking. Which does Redwood recommend for minimum risk and verifiable audit trails?
- Are there existing playbooks or sample MAPs (mutual action plans) and a way to run a staged purge in a sandbox to validate?

Can you send a short matrix that maps each option to operational implications (latency, cost, auditability, recovery limitations)? Also, please attach any SOC2 / architecture evidence we can use in our internal review.

Appreciate a concise set of options + recommended path for a regulated health workload.

Thanks,
Raj Patel
Head of Cloud Integrations
Healix Health

Raj — thanks, this is helpful context. I pulled the succinct answers together and attached a short matrix (data-retention-matrix.csv) and a redaction patterns primer (redaction-patterns.md). Below is a practical breakdown and recommended path for regulated PHI/PII.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- Retention caps: Hosted defaults are 30 days for ephemeral request logs and 90 days for longer analytic traces; we can contractually cap PHI to a shorter window (e.g., 90 days) for Hosted but backups may require an exception window. Dedicated and Private allow you to set retention policies to meet 0-365+ day windows at the tenant level; Private gives you the most control (you control snapshots).
- Purge SLA: Hosted: purge request queued and executed (hot store + async cache flush) within 72 hours; backups and cross-region snapshots: up to 30 days to fully scrub depending on snapshot lifecycle. Dedicated: typical SLA 72–120 hours depending on commit terms; Private: customer-managed, can be immediate if you operate your own snapshot lifecycle. We can put tighter SLAs into contract for enterprise accounts.
- Redaction recommendations: for highest assurance, combine client-side pre-ingest stripping (never send PHI) + deterministic pseudonymization for searchable fields (hashing with customer-owned salt). Server-side ingest redaction is possible (regex + named-entity filters) but is less auditable unless you also log pre/post checks. Inference-time masking is achievable via pre-processing hooks in Private and Dedicated (we can drop tokens before tokenization), but note that some features (e.g., semantic search or reranking) may require non-PHI context.

Operational tradeoffs (brief):
- Client-side stripping: latency 0, cost 0, auditability high (you control raw data), downside: you may lose utility for context-aware models.
- Deterministic hashing/pseudonymization: low latency, searchable, audit trail requires salt management, risk: poor hashing choices can be reversible if salts leak.
- Server-side regex/NLP redaction: medium latency, easier to centralize, needs robust QA to avoid leakage.
- Inference-time masking (pre-tokenization): preserves model utility while keeping PHI out of storage but requires Private/Dedicated hooks for safe implementation.

Backups & legal hold notes:
- Hosted backups: incremental snapshots retained on 30-day cycle by default. Purges are best-effort beyond the hot data purge; we can provide attestation when a purge completes.
- Legal hold: any legal hold will suspend purge actions until release; we recommend documenting expected processes and SLAs in the MAP.

Recommended path:
1) Scoping call (30 min) to review your data map and determine which fields must be treated as PHI vs metadata.
2) Decide deployment mode: Private if you need immediate purge control; Dedicated if you want Redwood-managed infra with stronger contractual SLAs; Hosted if you accept our standard backup windows.
3) Run a staged purge in a sandbox tenant (we’ll provide a checklist + logs).
4) Add contractual retention caps and backup scrubbing SLA to the SOW.

I attached the matrix and a short redaction patterns doc. Monica and Vivek are on this thread to help scope: Monica will coordinate the MAP and Vivek will outline the technical purge plan and audit artifacts we can provide.

Next step: what times work this week for a 30-minute scoping call?

Best,
Irene Choi

Thanks Irene — couple quick clarifications before we schedule: 
1) Audit logs: what retention is configurable for event/audit logs, and can we route logs to our own Splunk/CloudWatch so we can run independent verification after a purge?
2) Inference-time masking: you mentioned dropping tokens before tokenization. Is that available on Hosted (via a pre-processor webhook) or only on Dedicated/Private? We want to ensure the model never sees raw PHI even transiently.
3) Backups: if we ask to remove all PHI for a particular customer, is the 30-day backup window a hard technical limit for Hosted (i.e., will we still see traces for up to 30 days)?

If you can confirm those three items briefly we’ll pick a slot.

—Raj

Subject: Re: Clarifying PHI/PII retention caps and redaction options - Next steps

Raj — short answers below and next actions.

1) Audit logs: retention for audit/event logs is configurable per account in Dedicated/Private. Hosted default is 90 days for audit trails; you can export logs in real time to your SIEM (Splunk/CloudWatch) via our Log Forwarder integration — we strongly recommend exporting before you perform a purge so you retain an independent proof-of-action.

2) Inference-time masking: Hosted currently does NOT support arbitrary pre-tokenization webhooks for user-supplied code (we restrict execution surface for security). You can achieve masking on Hosted by performing client-side redaction or by using our deterministic pseudonymization API prior to sending data. Dedicated/Private support pre-processing hooks and token-level stripping so the model never receives raw PHI. In private deployments, you can drop fields at the edge (gateway) and apply enterprise KMS for hashing salts.

3) Backups: the 30-day window for Hosted snapshots is a typical operational window not a hard immutability guarantee — it reflects snapshot lifecycle. Practically, Hosted customers should assume that traces may exist in snapshots for up to 30 days; we provide attestation when a targeted purge completes and we remove data from hot stores and request snapshot scrub. If you need an absolute shorter backup exposure, Dedicated with contractual snapshot policies or Private where you control snapshots is the path.

Next actions I propose:
- Monica will send a one-page MAP template and a calendar invite for a 30-minute scoping call.
- Vivek will provision a sandbox tenant and a sample purge runbook; we’ll run a redaction + purge exercise and provide logs and a signed attestation.

I’ll include the attachments again. Let me know preferred times and we’ll book the call.

Regards,
Irene

Redwood Inference
